reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BitClub membership and paid mining-pool participation at prices from $99 to $3,500, while linking account credits, provisioning payments, team sales, and account cycles to bonuses. It encourages adding members and presents a claim of up to $2,000 daily per account. The $2 million monthly figure is described as a team result rather than a guaranteed future return, and the e-wallet link and tablet amount are not established as a promised return or completed outcome.

citations.quote: Pool 1 costs you $500
For every pool participation, Bitplot accesses IT hardware that will be integrated in our mining facility.
The Cycle Bonus is paid every 24 hours and is a significant portion of your income
Club's system is based on a binary structure
immediate payment pays 5 to 8 % on each purchase of new Participations by members of your team

opening.argument: The presentation does not establish a guaranteed result or conceal uncertainty. Its own language makes earning conditional: it says that, by becoming a member, viewers have an opportunity to generate money only “if you dedicates yourself,” while the description asks whether viewers seek a company that is “not a scam or leaves doubts.” The material therefore supports investigation and personal judgment rather than proving deceptive certainty. Claims about possible earnings should be treated as promotional examples, not as a promise that every viewer will receive them.

citations.quote: if you dedicates yourself you have the opportunity to generate unimaginable sums
Are you looking for a reliable company that is not a scam or leaves doubts about its activity, presence, or who its owner is?

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited prices and bonuses show a commercial offer, but they do not by themselves establish deception. “Paid every 24 hours” describes the stated timing of one bonus, not a guaranteed return on a viewer’s investment, and the binary structure describes organization rather than proof that losses or nonpayment are concealed. The reference also concedes that the $2 million statement concerns the team, not a promised individual result.

citations.quote: The Cycle Bonus is paid every 24 hours and is a significant portion of your income
Club's system is based on a binary structure

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The conditional wording does not neutralize the concrete earnings pitch. The presentation gives specific pool prices, recurring bonus descriptions, and a claimed daily figure, so a reasonable viewer is being encouraged to expect financial gain, not merely warned to investigate. The phrase “opportunity” still promotes the offer and does not disclose a meaningful risk of loss or explain whether the claimed figures are independently verified.

citations.quote: Pool 1 costs you $500
that would bring you up to 2,000 dollars daily for each account
As you can see, your three top accounts are making money without you doing anything.

opening.argument: The format is plausibly an educational walkthrough of how the platform is structured, not proof of a completed solicitation or fraudulent outcome. The speaker explicitly calls the material “informative videos,” says that the videos show viewers how to do it, and invites them to watch accounts developing live in webinars. The account-tree diagrams and pool illustrations can therefore be read as demonstrations of a business model and its arithmetic. Explaining how a system claims to work is not the same as independently certifying that the claims are true.

citations.quote: through these informative videos
In our videos we show you how to do it
watch every Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, how your accounts are developing live

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material informative does not change what it teaches. The walkthrough explains how to activate accounts, add members, place them in a binary tree, and derive payments from the resulting credits. That is operational recruitment guidance tied to compensation, not neutral technology education. The live-webinar invitation likewise directs viewers toward the promoted system rather than supplying independent scrutiny.

citations.quote: All you have to do is to pass the information
sales are generated which get translated to the following discounts
immediate payment pays 5 to 8 % on each purchase of new Participations by members of your team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is part of the sales pitch, not a defense against it. The lesson tells viewers how to join, expand accounts, recruit members, and calculate earnings; the diagrams make that mechanism easier to follow. A tutorial can still promote a scam when its subject is paid participation and recruitment-linked rewards, especially where the presentation supplies attractive outcomes without reliable verification.

citations.quote: you have the chance to location another account on the left leg and another one on the right
Now it's time to add other members of the Club
you would also charge an immediate bonus of some $ 1,000

opening.argument: The observable offer can be characterized as membership, hardware access, and a described referral service, while several decisive scam mechanisms are not established. The speaker says participation accesses IT hardware integrated into a mining facility, and the presentation lists concrete pool prices and credits. But the supplied material does not establish a credential request, a completed payout, or that any individual was actually induced to transfer funds. Even the ambiguous reference to documents is framed as an optional link action, not proof of identity theft. Those gaps support treating this as ordinary, if highly speculative, commerce rather than proving a scam.

citations.quote: For every pool participation, Bitplot accesses IT hardware that will be integrated in our mining facility.
Pool 1 costs you $500
If you want to use one or more of your documents, do not hesitate to click on the link in the description.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce framing omits the central compensation mechanism. The offer is not merely hardware for sale: it ties participation to credits, recurring cycle payments, team-member purchases, and multiple accounts. A completed payout or credential theft is unnecessary to identify the promoted mechanism; the problem is the solicitation of money through mining and recruitment-linked returns, not only an already-proven victim outcome.

citations.quote: The Cycle Bonus is paid every 24 hours and is a significant portion of your income
each purchase of new Participations by members of your team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-outcome argument is too narrow. The video itself presents paid mining participation, recurring Bitcoin bonuses, and a binary account structure in which team activity generates compensation. Those are not ordinary retail features merely because the material does not show a particular victim or completed withdrawal. Hardware imagery cannot verify ownership, capacity, or the promised economics, and the presentation does not substantiate that the advertised service actually produces the stated returns.
